pool.title: PAMELA Measurements of Cosmic-Ray Proton and Helium Spectra
pool.why: The direct-detection result that opened the modern picture: precise 1 GV-1.2 TV proton and helium spectra that cannot be fit by single power laws, revealing the ~230-240 GV spectral hardening and the harder-than-proton helium slope — the canonical 'break' any review of this need must cite.

pool.title: Precision Measurement of the Proton Flux in Primary Cosmic Rays from Rigidity 1 GV to 1.8 TV with the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer on the International Space Station
pool.why: The AMS-02 benchmark proton spectrum that confirmed and sharply resolved the high-rigidity hardening (progressive index change), defining the current observational proton picture the researcher is reviewing.

pool.title: Precision Measurement of the Helium Flux in Primary Cosmic Rays of Rigidities 1.9 GV to 3 TV with the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer on the International Space Station
pool.why: The companion AMS-02 helium spectrum showing the same >100 GV hardening and quantifying the proton/helium spectral-index difference — a core tension (different p and He slopes) the need asks about.

pool.title: Cosmic-Ray Electron Flux Measured by the PAMELA Experiment between 1 and 625 GeV
pool.why: The landmark space-borne electron-only spectrum (1-625 GeV) that establishes the direct-detection electron picture the need explicitly requests, and the reference point against which later spectral features are judged.

pool.title: An anomalous positron abundance in cosmic rays with energies 1.5-100 GeV
pool.why: The flagship tension revealed by direct detection: the PAMELA positron excess above 10 GeV that departs from secondary-production expectations — the single most-cited 'anomaly' a review of PAMELA/AMS spectra and their tensions cannot omit.

pool.title: Cosmic-Ray Proton and Helium Spectra from the First CREAM Flight
pool.why: The premier balloon-borne (the need names balloon experiments) high-energy proton/helium measurement that independently exposed the spectral hardening and the harder helium spectrum at TeV energies, corroborating PAMELA/AMS from a different instrument.

pool.title: Voyager 1 Observes Low-Energy Galactic Cosmic Rays in a Region Depleted of Heliospheric Ions
pool.why: The heliopause-crossing paper reporting the first in-situ galactic cosmic-ray H, He, and electron spectra outside the heliosphere — the direct measurement of the unmodulated input the need centers on.

pool.title: Galactic Cosmic Rays in the Local Interstellar Medium: Voyager 1 Observations and Model Results
pool.why: The definitive Voyager 1 local interstellar spectra (H, He, electrons down to a few MeV/nuc) presented explicitly as the LIS input for modulation models — precisely how Voyager constrains the unmodulated spectrum that the researcher wants to explain.

pool.title: The acceleration of cosmic rays in shock fronts - I
pool.why: One of the two founding formulations (microscopic/kinetic view) of diffusive shock acceleration, the mechanism the intent names explicitly; no survey of CR acceleration can omit it.

pool.title: Particle acceleration by astrophysical shocks
pool.why: The companion founding paper on diffusive shock (first-order Fermi) acceleration deriving the universal power-law spectrum; canonically cited alongside Bell as the origin of the standard acceleration paradigm.

pool.title: An introduction to the theory of diffusive shock acceleration of energetic particles in tenuous plasmas
pool.why: The canonical review/derivation of DSA theory that every related-work section cites as the pedagogical anchor for the acceleration mechanism.

pool.title: Particle acceleration at astrophysical shocks: A theory of cosmic ray origin
pool.why: The landmark Physics Reports synthesis explicitly linking shock acceleration to the origin of galactic cosmic rays — the reference tying 'acceleration mechanism' to 'CR origin' the intent asks for.

pool.title: The Effect of Wave-Particle Interactions on the Propagation of Cosmic Rays
pool.why: The foundational treatment of the cosmic-ray streaming instability and self-generated Alfven-wave scattering — the microphysical basis of CR diffusion and confinement in the interstellar medium.

pool.title: Cosmic-Ray Propagation and Interactions in the Galaxy
pool.why: The definitive review of galactic CR propagation modeling (diffusion, halo, secondary production, GALPROP) — the single most indispensable reference for the transport half of the intent.

pool.title: Detection of the Characteristic Pion-Decay Signature in Supernova Remnants
pool.why: The decisive gamma-ray measurement (pion bump in IC 443 and W44) proving hadronic CR proton acceleration in supernova remnants — the observational cornerstone linking gamma-rays to acceleration theory.

pool.title: Precision Measurement of the Proton Flux in Primary Cosmic Rays from Rigidity 1 GV to 1.8 TV with the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer on the International Space Station
pool.why: The flagship precision direct CR-flux measurement revealing the proton spectral hardening that reshaped transport/acceleration models — the canonical 'CR-flux measurement' evidence the intent requires.

pool.why: The founding observation of the field: it reported the anomalous low-energy enhancement (helium) at 1 AU that cannot be explained by conventional modulation and that defines ACRs; any state-of-the-art summary of ACRs must trace the phenomenon to this discovery.

pool.title: An interpretation of the observed oxygen and nitrogen enhancements in low-energy cosmic rays
pool.why: The canonical origin hypothesis — ACRs are interstellar neutrals that enter the heliosphere, are ionized to pickup ions, and are then accelerated; this is the physical starting point for all the acceleration and transport models the need asks about.

pool.title: Cosmic ray drift, shock wave acceleration, and the anomalous component of cosmic rays
pool.why: The canonical acceleration formulation the heliosheath debate is defined against: diffusive shock acceleration of pickup ions at the solar-wind termination shock as the ACR source, with drifts explaining the observed gradients and solar-cycle behavior.

Potgieter 2013 — Solar Modulation of Cosmic Rays

pool.title: The passage of energetic charged particles through interplanetary space
pool.why: Introduces the Parker cosmic-ray transport equation — the foundational framework (diffusion, convection, drift, adiabatic energy change) for modeling particle transport and modulation throughout the heliosphere, indispensable for the modulation-in-the-outermost-heliosphere prong of the need.

pool.title: Voyager 1 explores the termination shock region and the heliosheath beyond
pool.why: The decisive in-situ measurement: Voyager 1's termination-shock crossing showed ACR helium intensity did NOT peak at the shock, creating the 'Voyager paradox' that reframed where and how ACRs are accelerated in the heliosheath.

pool.title: An asymmetric solar wind termination shock
pool.why: The Voyager 2 termination-shock crossing confirmed at a second, asymmetric location that the ACR source is again not at the shock — the second decisive measurement driving the shift toward heliosheath / off-nose acceleration models.
source_reviews: Giacalone et al. 2022 — Anomalous Cosmic Rays and Heliospheric Energetic Particles
Potgieter 2013 — Solar Modulation of Cosmic Rays

pool.title: An explanation of the Voyager paradox: Particle acceleration at a blunt termination shock
pool.why: The leading model reconciling the paradox with shock acceleration: blunt-shock geometry moves the effective ACR acceleration site to the flanks (longer field-line connection times), explaining why Voyager saw no ACR source at the nose.

pool.title: The acceleration of anomalous cosmic rays by stochastic acceleration in the heliosheath
pool.why: The canonical non-shock alternative: stochastic / pump acceleration that redistributes pickup-ion energy into a suprathermal ACR tail distributed through the heliosheath volume — a leading answer to 'what accelerates ACRs beyond the termination shock.'

pool.title: A magnetic reconnection mechanism for the generation of anomalous cosmic rays

pool.title: Time dependence of the proton flux measured by PAMELA during the 2006 July - 2009 December solar minimum

pool.title: Time Dependence of the Electron and Positron Components of the Cosmic Radiation Measured by the PAMELA Experiment between July 2006 and December 2015

pool.title: Observation of Fine Time Structures in the Cosmic Proton and Helium Fluxes with the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer on the International Space Station

pool.title: Effects of particle drift on cosmic-ray transport. I. General properties, application to solar modulation

pool.title: Solar Modulation of Galactic Cosmic Rays

pool.title: The passage of energetic charged particles through interplanetary space
pool.why: Derives the cosmic-ray transport (Parker) equation underpinning all heliospheric modulation theory; a related-work section grounded in modulation observations cannot skip the framework against which the time-dependent data are interpreted.

pool.why: The definitive review/tutorial of the SDE method for energetic-particle and cosmic-ray transport; it IS the 'overview of SDE approaches' the need asks for, walking through the Fokker-Planck/Parker to SDE reformulation, time-forward vs time-backward integration, pseudo-particle interpretation, and numerical schemes vs finite-difference. Any competent search for this need must return it as a top hit.

pool.title: A stochastic view of the solar modulation phenomena of cosmic rays
pool.why: The first paper to recast the cosmic-ray solar-modulation Fokker-Planck equation as Ito stochastic differential equations solved with pseudo-particles (1D); the historical origin point any SDE-methods related-work section cannot skip, and the source of the arrival-time / energy-loss distribution insight.
source_reviews: Strauss & Effenberger 2017 (named as the first SDE-based GCR modulation model)

pool.title: A Markov Stochastic Process Theory of Cosmic-Ray Modulation
pool.why: Established the Markov-stochastic-process (time-backward) formulation of the full 3D transport equation including particle drift, giving the canonical backward-in-time SDE framework that underpins most modern heliospheric modulation solvers.

pool.title: A general time-dependent stochastic method for solving Parker's transport equation in spherical coordinates
pool.why: First general time-dependent 3D stochastic solution of Parker's transport equation in spherical coordinates, and the review's showcase benchmarking study of the SDE solver against finite-difference solutions — directly the numerical accuracy / cost trade-off the need calls out.
source_reviews: Strauss & Effenberger 2017 (used as the SDE-vs-finite-difference benchmarking example)

pool.title: A stochastic differential equation code for multidimensional Fokker-Planck type problems
pool.why: The widely used general-purpose multidimensional SDE code; it documents how forward vs backward integration corresponds to different Fokker-Planck forms and argues the unconditional stability / accuracy advantage of the SDE approach over operator-splitting finite-difference schemes — squarely the methods content the need requests.
source_reviews: Strauss & Effenberger 2017 (cited for the detailed forward/backward SDE formulation)

pool.title: On the forward-backward-in-time approach for Monte Carlo solution of Parker's transport equation: One-dimensional case
pool.why: A head-to-head study of time-forward vs time-backward stochastic integration for Parker's equation, quantifying each scheme's systematic accuracy against the Crank-Nicolson finite-difference solution — precisely the forward/backward-scheme and accuracy-vs-finite-difference comparison the need specifies.
source_reviews: Strauss & Effenberger 2017 (cited as the reference comparing time-forward and time-backward approaches)

pool.title: The Two Sources of Solar Energetic Particles

pool.title: Associations between coronal mass ejections and solar energetic proton events

pool.title: Shock Geometry, Seed Populations, and the Origin of Variable Elemental Composition at High Energies in Large Gradual Solar Particle Events
pool.why: Landmark explaining why high-energy (GLE-range) gradual-SEP spectra and composition vary, via shock geometry plus mixed flare/solar-wind seed populations — central to understanding the spectra neutron monitors sample.

pool.title: Large gradual solar energetic particle events
pool.why: The definitive modern Living Review of large gradual SEP events — the very class that produces GLEs; the anchor review an SEP/GLE introduction cannot omit.

pool.title: Acceleration and Propagation of Solar Energetic Particles
pool.why: Comprehensive review of SEP acceleration at flares and CME-driven shocks plus interplanetary transport — directly serves the 'acceleration and origin mechanisms' summary the intro requires.

pool.title: Three Unusual Cosmic-Ray Increases Possibly Due to Charged Particles from the Sun
pool.why: The discovery paper of ground-level enhancements — the first detection of solar particles at ground/neutron-monitor level; the historical origin point for how GLEs are observed.

pool.title: Solar Cosmic Rays of February, 1956 and Their Propagation through Interplanetary Space
pool.why: Definitive study of GLE05 (23 Feb 1956), the largest GLE ever recorded, reconstructing the proton rigidity spectrum from the neutron-monitor network — squarely the 'largest historical event' plus 'spectra from neutron monitors' need.

pool.title: The Cosmic Ray Nucleonic Component: The Invention and Scientific Uses of the Neutron Monitor
pool.why: The canonical reference for the neutron monitor itself — the instrument through which GLEs are detected and their energy spectra are derived.

pool.title: The October 22, 1989, solar cosmic ray enhancement: An analysis of the anisotropy and spectral characteristics
pool.why: Classic demonstration of deriving SEP energy spectra, anisotropy and pitch-angle distributions from the global neutron-monitor network — the methodological landmark for reconstructing GLE spectra from neutron monitors.

pool.title: Extreme solar events

pool.title: End to the Cosmic-Ray Spectrum?
pool.why: The canonical prediction of the GZK cutoff (proton attenuation on the CMB); any account of the current understanding of the UHECR energy spectrum must return it as the theoretical origin of the observed flux suppression.

pool.title: The Origin of Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays

pool.title: A Heitler model of extensive air showers
